chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man dies leaving his wife, and he had not yet consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the full dowry if he had specified a dowry for her, and she receives a share of the inheritance. And if he had not specified a dowry for her, she has no dowry, but she receives the inheritance."

key_terms.عَنِ اِمْرَأَتِهِ: leaving his wife / from the perspective of his wife

ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights of a wife if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib*, clarifies the dual entitlement of a wife whose husband dies before consummation: she retains her full dowry (*mahr*) as a vested right and simultaneously inherits as a surviving spouse. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that death before *dakhil* (consummation) does not negate the marriage contract's financial obligations, distinguishing it from divorce scenarios where the dowry may be reduced. The hadith reinforces the principle that inheritance rights are triggered by the existence of the contract, while dowry rights are secured by the naming of the amount.
